column1: # shows.tsv -- the standing feed's show table. One row per podcast.
# feed-update.sh reads this. Adding a show is a row here and nothing else:
# no code change, no new unit, no new timer.
# TAB-SEPARATED. Seven required fields plus one optional eighth. Blank lines
# and #-comments are ignored. The literal string $HOME is expanded by the
# script, so paths stay portable and this file carries no username.
#   slug         short id, used only in log lines
#   feed         RSS feed URL, passed straight to yt-dlp
#   audio_dir    where mp3s and .info.json sidecars land
#   archive      yt-dlp --download-archive file; this is what stops re-downloads
#   ledger       bulk-transcribe.sh resume ledger: mp3 filename -> job UUID
#   outdir       where export-transcripts.sh writes .json and .txt
#   profile_id   Scriberr transcription profile applied to THIS show's jobs
#   ytflags      OPTIONAL. Extra yt-dlp flags, space separated.
# WHY THE EIGHTH FIELD EXISTS -- yt-dlp PICKS AN EXTRACTOR BY URL AND SOME OF
# THEM SILENTLY RETURN NOTHING. Art19 (`https://rss.art19.com/...`) has a
# dedicated `Art19Show` extractor that reports `Downloading 0 items` on a plain
# RSS feed, with no error and exit 0. Captivate has no dedicated extractor, so
# it falls through to `generic`, which parses the enclosures and works. Force
# the fallback with `--use-extractors generic` (or `--force-generic-extractor`
# on older builds; both work on yt-dlp 2026.07.04). If a new show pulls zero
# episodes and the run still reports errors=0, THIS is the first thing to check:
#     curl -sL "<FEED>" | grep -c "<enclosure"
# A non-zero count with a zero-item playlist means the extractor, not the feed.
# `--playlist-items 1:300` also belongs here when a back catalogue is not worth
# its GPU time. Feeds are newest-first, so that takes the most recent 300.
# KEEP THE LEDGER OUT OF audio_dir. Clearing tens of GB of audio someday should
# not take the resume record with it.
# WHY EVERY PATH IS SPELLED OUT INSTEAD OF DERIVED FROM THE SLUG:
#   Do This NOT That already has 634 episodes recorded in a ledger at
#   $HOME/podcasts/.transcribed.tsv and 634 pairs of files in a flat
#   transcripts/ directory. Deriving paths from the slug would point
#   bulk-transcribe.sh at an empty ledger, and it would cheerfully re-transcribe
#   the entire back catalogue. Explicit paths keep the existing corpus untouched.
# WHEN SHOW #2 ARRIVES: give it a per-show subdirectory under transcripts/.
#   The flat directory is a legacy of there having been exactly one show, and
#   two shows in one directory means filename collisions are possible and the
#   output carries no show identity. Whether to also move show #1's 634 pairs
#   down into a subdirectory is a decision for that day, not a default.
# PER-SHOW PROFILES ARE THE POINT.
#   Sortformer caps at 4 speakers; a panel show past that needs a pyannote
#   profile instead. A solo-monologue show wants a different max-speaker bound
#   than a two-host show. This column is why the CLI watcher was rejected --
#   it applies one server-wide default profile to everything it uploads.
#slug
dtnt
martech
